Bug_Title: SIC: Deadly embrace of non-static inner class and thread local (SIC_THREADLOCAL_DEADLY_EMBRACE)
Bug_Details:
This class is an inner class, but should probably be a static inner class.
  As it is, there is a serious danger of a deadly embrace between the inner class
  and the thread local in the outer class. Because the inner class isn't static,
  it retains a reference to the outer class.
  If the thread local contains a reference to an instance of the inner
  class, the inner and outer instance will both be reachable
  and not eligible for garbage collection.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by defining 'InnerClass' as a non-static inner class. This means each instance of 'InnerClass' holds a reference to its enclosing 'DeadlyEmbraceExample' instance. When 'threadLocal' holds a reference to an 'InnerClass' instance, both the 'InnerClass' instance and its enclosing 'DeadlyEmbraceExample' instance become unreachable and ineligible for garbage collection, leading to a memory leak.
Trigger_Explanation: The test triggers the bug by calling the `showBug` method of the `DeadlyEmbraceExample` class. This method creates an instance of the non-static inner class `InnerClass` and sets it in a `ThreadLocal`, creating a deadly embrace that prevents garbage collection of both the inner and outer class instances.
